[i]Thanks to the weather, the ninth mechanized battalion managed to avoid the brunt of what would've been a beyond lethal artillery barrage. The combination of strong winds, fog, rain, and possibly lacking proper training with the old equipment they had made it so that the creeping barrage was several meters off target. Though the combination of cluster munitions with conventional shells made it so that at least something was struck with stray bomblets. But it quickly subsided as the carnage migrated away from them into a nearby forest. [/i]

[quote=stuipendia;61399962]The great hum is the first thing she notices; it sounds like a computer, no, a hundred thousand servers performing a great hymn. A call to something beyond this world, to the Mechanical Hyperuranion. A manufactured divinity, the waiting and the man-made. Before us, and formed from our hubris. She feels watched, the cameras leer at her, yes, and the locals are aware of her dress but are unquestioning of Li and his calling to a foreign Imperium. But this was something else entirely. She was not talked to, excluding the airport attendants, even then they seemed stiff. But here, this tower, the Freed Workers Tower, it screams. It sings hymns, not to her God, perhaps not to any God, but its existence worshipped something. It had to. A veritable Tower of Babel.

As she walked in the door, it got louder; the secretary greeted her. Stiff, like an automaton. 

[i]"Ah, you must be the Keeper, yes? [u][b]He[/b][/u] will see you now, just step into the elevator!"[/i]

The elevator was emblazoned with the sigil of Technocratic Socialism.[/quote]
She walked, undisturbed by the lack of conversation, through the path assigned to her by her superiors. It did seem odd, but she was accustomed to moving through the world on her own.

Agnieszka nodded and stepped into the elevator, going up high to the floor she had been indicated. Now she was alone with the sound of humming machines, their presence simultaneously overbearing and a comforting white noise. It reminded her of the resonance beneath the lower sanctum of the Nexite Church in Solaria, where the bones of saints lay in perfect peace and the fountains of affliction had run dry. Only that this was different, it was nothing like the holy pursuit of knowledge she had dedicated her life to. If it were up to her, it would be called-

Her thoughts were interrupted by the ding of the elevator. The doors slid open, and she stepped out.
